decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 3322, so no exact-duplicate removal step is needed.
tailnum has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 3322 exactly equal to row_count 3322, making it the only column that plausibly identifies one row per plane.
All sampled year values (1956.0 ... 2013.0) are integral with no fractional component, justifying a cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.
distinct_values for engines are exactly {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}, an integral count justifying a cast to INTEGER.
seats ranges from min 2.0 to max 450.0 with all samples integral, justifying a cast to INTEGER.
speed's 13 distinct_values are all integral (90.0 to 432.0) so it casts to INTEGER, but null_rate 0.993076 means it is retained nullable rather than imputed.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true and carry no business meaning.
year has null_rate 0.021072 (70 of 3322 rows), a modest but real gap that must not be imputed or dropped.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null), so the column is kept but flagged as sparsely populated rather than dropped or imputed.

purpose: This table provides a cleaned registry of aircraft (one row per tail number) with physical and manufacturing attributes, feeding downstream flight-analysis joins that need plane characteristics such as manufacturer, model, engine type, and seating capacity.
usage: Join on tailnum to enrich flight records with aircraft attributes; treat year and speed as nullable and filter or coalesce them explicitly before aggregation, since speed is populated for well under 1% of rows.
limitations: Three Airbyte capture-metadata columns were dropped entirely; year is missing for about 2.1% of rows and speed is missing for about 99.3% of rows and neither gap was imputed, so any analysis depending on those fields will be based on a small, non-random subset of planes.
